patterns: Handwriting as proof that a person showed up: Dan Mall's thank-you notes, 'a long message without AI is the new handwritten letter,' copywork by hand, and a Flutter package that fakes real pen ink all landed on the same day.
Reading slumps are everywhere today, and the AO3 outage is pushing a lot of fanfic readers back to books. Questions about what breaks a slump get answers.
Big-account energy is about uncertainty and taste: James Clear on a mindset that handles uncertainty (~117k), Yongfook asking what dictation apps add (~60k, 118 replies).
Mental health talk on the watchlist is clinical and blunt (Awais Aftab on BPD discourse, ~39k). Outside it, people describe journaling as the thing that helps.
Fountain Pen Day wishlists are starting to show up ahead of next week, mostly from retailers, so a personal, non-shopping pen post stands out.
Sketchbook tours and letterpress studios get strong likes for small accounts when the post is just the pages.

reply_ideas.description: Dan Mall on two handwritten thank-you notes carried around all month, asking who you've been meaning to thank
reply_ideas.reply_text: What gets me is that you'd been carrying both notes around all month. A text gets read once, but a card ends up in a coat pocket. Are you writing your thank-yous by hand this weekend too, or does that put too much pressure on the first one?

reply_ideas.description: Emma Twersky, a Google developer relations lead, sharing a Flutter package called fountain_pen that makes on-screen handwriting look like real pen ink
reply_ideas.reply_text: I love that someone took the trouble to make digital ink look like it came from a nib instead of a marker. Does the stroke change with speed, the way a fountain pen lays down more ink when you slow down?

reply_ideas.description: a writer who has handwritten the best ads and posts they find every day for four weeks to learn the craft
reply_ideas.reply_text: Copying good writing by hand works because your hand can't skim. Have you noticed a pattern in which ones you pick? After four weeks I'd guess that notebook says as much about your taste as it does about the ads.

bip_draft:
This week on Calmly Crashing I'm still writing the filled-in examples for the Smaller Start Kit. Every page gets one, so nobody has to face a blank worksheet on a day when everything already feels like too much.

#buildinpublic
video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Overhead on textured cream paper, a hand writes a short thank-you card with a fountain pen, blots it, and slides it into an envelope. Pen and paper sounds only, no music. End on a card that reads 'Who are you writing to?' Pairs with the thank-you note post.

x_posts.title: The thank-you note
x_posts.text:
Who's the person you keep meaning to write a thank-you note to?

I don't think the card has to be good. It just has to get mailed before you talk yourself out of sending it.
x_posts.why: handwritten-thanks cluster (Dan Mall's notes, 'the new handwritten letter')

x_posts.title: Slow on purpose
x_posts.text: Someone said today that a long message written without AI is the new handwritten letter. I write by hand every day, and what I'd miss most is how slow it is. My hand never gets far enough ahead of me to say something I don't mean.
x_posts.why: 'a long message without AI is the new handwritten letter' plus copywork by hand
